text:
Cole Hutson was a second-round pick, 43rd overall in 2024, and his big brother Lane won the Calder Trophy. Twenty-one games into his first full NHL season, Cole has his own rookie headlines: RMNB had him leading all rookies in scoring after a three-assist night against New Jersey on Nov. 14, and Daily Faceoff called his rise surprising. He has 5 goals and 15 points, 5 of them on the power play, on 19.67 minutes a night at age 20.

Most of it looks real. His own chances come at 0.63 expected goals per 60 (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and Washington controls play at five on five with him on. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking spots a signature in six games: 33% of his setups go across the royal road, against 4% for a typical defenseman. Our numbers put his true scoring rate a little lower, 1.91 points per 60 against 2.18 now, and project about 55 points. The worry is the team around him, which has lost five straight. He also took a shot off his right foot on Nov. 19, per NHL.com's Tom Gulitti, and played in Boston two nights later.
headline: Cole Hutson is making the family name his own
